result.title: Model Immunization Cannot Reliably Protect Models from Harmful Adaptation
result.summary: Efficient fine-tuning techniques have substantially reduced the cost of adapting open-weight models, enabling malicious actors to readily fine-tune them toward harmful capabilities. In response, model immunization modifies a pretrained checkpoint to resist subsequent adaptation toward designated harmful capabilities while preserving its utility and adaptability for benign tasks. Furthermore, a few immunization methods have sought to keep their protection robust to some changes in the attacker's adaptation. However, fine-tuning offers attackers many more low-cost options, and we observe that existing methods still substantially overfit to the attacker configuration they are optimized against. Such overfitting stays hidden when immunization is evaluated under, or near, this configuration, so the reported protection may give a false sense of security. To rigorously evaluate model immunization, we conduct experiments, varying one component of this configuration at a time: the harmful data, the adaptation strategy, or the model initialization. Across four immunization methods on text-to-image generation and image classification, with additional results on language models, these variations substantially degrade the protection, and in many cases the immunized model relearns the harmful capability nearly as well as the un-immunized model. Existing immunization therefore cannot reliably protect models, leaving them vulnerable to harmful adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验「模型免疫」——修改预训练 checkpoint 使其抵抗后续有害能力微调、同时保留良性任务效用——是否真的稳健：在文生图、图像分类及语言模型上分别改变有害数据、适配策略与初始化，发现四种免疫方法的保护都大幅失效，甚至接近未免疫模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心发现是训练期干预只对特定配置有效、在被优化的配置附近评测会掩盖过拟合，这一评测视角可能可供核查 LVR 的轨迹训练与监督是否也过度拟合单一设置；但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理状态，联系较弱。
